description.value: Walk-in wilderness campsite at a sweeping white-sand bay on the southern edge of Cape Scott Provincial Park, reached by an easy trail through old-growth Sitka spruce and cedar; the trailhead is at the end of an active logging road with truck traffic.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM record tags San Josef Bay Campsite as a camp_site and links to the BC Parks Cape Scott Park page, which was successfully fetched. The website confirms Cape Scott Park is an active wilderness park at the northwestern tip of Vancouver Island, explicitly naming San Josef Bay as one of its significant beaches and camping areas. No campsite-specific amenity details are provided in the website content; the park is described throughout as a remote wilderness area, and the site appears accessible only by hiking trail rather than by road or bicycle.
concerns: Campsite appears to be backcountry wilderness accessible only by foot trail, not by road or bicycle — suitability for a cycling tourism directory is unclear.
No address or phone number is available in OSM or on the BC Parks website for this specific campsite.
The linked BC Parks page covers all of Cape Scott Park and provides no amenity or access details specific to San Josef Bay Campsite.
OSM record has no address or contact details beyond the website URL.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: San Josef Bay Campsite is a legitimate, active BC Parks wilderness campsite, but it appears accessible only by hiking trail rather than by bicycle or vehicle, which limits its direct relevance to a cycling tourism directory. A human reviewer should confirm whether bikepacking or adventure cyclists regularly use this as a destination.
enrichment_extras.notes: The BC Parks website notes that tourist facilities (accommodation, food) are available in nearby communities including Port Hardy, Port McNeill, Holberg, and Port Alice, though these are distant from the remote campsite itself.
